## Description

Estimate a firm’s intangible capital from point-in-time R&D investment data (and test any additional SG&A capitalization separately), adjust book equity and profitability measures, then rank stocks on industry-relative adjusted valuation and profitability. A conservative long-only version owns a diversified basket of firms with attractive adjusted valuation and strong adjusted profitability; test annual versus quarterly rebalancing rather than assuming an optimal frequency.

## Where it may fit

Long-horizon equity investing; potentially useful when reported book value understates internally developed intangible assets. Not a hedge for every market regime.

## Vehicles

Diversified common-stock universe; long-only stock portfolio or research factor portfolio.

## Required data

Point-in-time financial statements; R&D expenses and other separately identified intangible-investment inputs; shares, prices, corporate actions, industry classification, and survivorship-free historical universe.

## Caveats

Published research motivates an intangibles factor but does not validate this specific adjusted-value/profitability hybrid. Capitalization life, expense categories, reporting lags, industry normalization, and rebalance settings must be fixed before testing. Use point-in-time data and include turnover, delistings, costs, and taxes.
